prose.before: Dearly beloved: Be humbled under the powerful hand of God, so that He may lift you up in the time of visitation, casting all your anxiety on Him, for He is concerned for you. Be sober and keep watch, because your adversary the devil circles about like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour. Resist him, strong in faith, aware that the same suffering comes upon your brotherhood that is in the world. And the God of all grace, who called us to His everlasting glory in Christ Jesus — He Himself will perfect, confirm and establish us, who have suffered for a short while. To Him be glory and dominion for ever and ever. Amen.

prose.before: Brethren: I entreat you not to falter in my tribulations for you, which is your glory. On this account I bend my knees before the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, from whom every fatherhood in the heavens and on earth is named, that He may give you, according to the riches of His glory, to be strengthened with might through His Spirit for the inner man, and that Christ may dwell by faith in your hearts; in order that you, rooted and founded in love, may be able to grasp what the breadth and the length and the loftiness and the depth are, together with all the saints, and to know also the love of Christ which surpasses knowledge, so that you may be filled to the whole fullness of God. And to Him who can do all things far more abundantly than we ask or understand, according to the power that works within us, to Him be glory within the Church and in Christ Jesus, to all generations, for ever and ever. Amen.

prose.before: In many portions and in many ways God spoke of old to the fathers in the prophets; at last, in these days, He has spoken to us in the Son, whom He established as heir of all things, through whom He also made the ages; who, being the splendor of His glory and the form of His substance, and bearing all things by His word of power, making the cleansing of sins, sits on high at the right hand of the Majesty, having been made as far superior to the angels as the name He has inherited is more distinguished than theirs. For to which of the angels did He ever say: You are my Son, today I have begotten You? And once more: I will be a father to Him, and He will be a son to me? And when He again brings the firstborn into the world, He says: And let all God’s angels adore Him. And concerning the angels He indeed says: Who makes His angels into spirits, and His ministers into a flame of fire. Yet to the Son: O God, Your throne is for ever and ever; the rod of Your kingdom is a rod of equity. You have loved justice and hated iniquity; for this reason God, Your God, has anointed You with the oil of exultation above those who share with You. And: You, O Lord, in the beginning founded the earth, and the works of Your hands are the heavens. They will perish, but You will remain; and they will all grow old like a garment, and like a mantle You will change them, and they will be changed; but You are the very same, and Your years will not fail.
